gloss: -year student; student in the nth year

definitions.gloss: student in the nth year (of a school)
definitions.explanation: Attached to a number to say what year of school someone is in: {一年生|いちねんせい} (first-year student), {三年生|さんねんせい} (third-year student). The school itself is understood from context or named separately.

examples.japanese: {弟|おとうと}は{三年生|さんねんせい}だ。
examples.english: My younger brother is a third-year student.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}の{一年生|いちねんせい}になった。
examples.english: She started first grade in elementary school.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}{四年生|よねんせい}は{就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}で{忙|いそが}しい。
examples.english: Fourth-year university students are busy with job hunting.

examples.japanese: {何年生|なんねんせい}ですかと{聞|き}かれて、{中学|ちゅうがく}{二年生|にねんせい}ですと{答|こた}えた。
examples.english: When asked what year I was in, I answered that I was in the second year of junior high.

notes:
From {年|ねん} (year) + {生|せい} (student). The number takes the on'yomi: いち, に, さん, よ ({四年生|よねんせい}), ご, ろく.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小学|しょうがく}{一年生|いちねんせい}: first-grader
- {高校|こうこう}{三年生|さんねんせい}: third-year high school student (final year)
- {何年生|なんねんせい}: what year (question word)
- {新|しん}{一年生|いちねんせい}: incoming first-year student

USAGE:
Japanese counts school years from one within each school, so a {中学|ちゅうがく}{一年生|いちねんせい} is a seventh-grader in American terms. The school year begins in April, so students change year in the spring.
